title: Rating Rule — Applying Cardinal DriveSense Adjustments to Vehicle Premium
content:
**Rule.** Cardinal DriveSense discounts and surcharges are applied vehicle by vehicle. Each enrolled vehicle's participation or earned adjustment lowers (or, for a surcharge, raises) that vehicle's share of the base premium only, before the policy-level surcharges and discounts of the auto rating are applied, and is never averaged across the policy or moved to another vehicle. A DriveSense adjustment is not part of the policy discount sum and does not count toward the maximum total discount of the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy package. A vehicle on a pay-per-mile program takes no participation or earned discount.

## The rule, part by part

| Point | What the rule fixes |
|---|---|
| What the adjustment acts on | The enrolled vehicle's own share of the base premium |
| Direction | A participation discount or an earned discount lowers that share; a surcharge raises it |
| When, within rating | Before the policy-level surcharges and discounts of the auto rating are applied |
| Across vehicles | Never averaged across the policy; never moved to another vehicle |
| Policy discount sum | A DriveSense adjustment is not part of it |
| Package maximum total discount | A DriveSense adjustment does not count toward it |
| Pay-per-mile programs (Cardinal DriveSense Miles Mobile, Cardinal DriveSense Miles Plug-In) | No participation discount and no earned discount |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

A policy has two vehicles. Vehicle A's share of the base premium is $600.00 and it carries a fixed earned discount of 15%; vehicle B's share is $500.00 and it is not enrolled.

- Vehicle A: 15% of $600.00 is $90.00, so its share becomes $600.00 less $90.00, which is $510.00.
- Vehicle B: its share stays $500.00. None of vehicle A's discount is spread to it.
- The policy-level surcharges and discounts of the auto rating are then applied to shares of $510.00 and $500.00.

Had vehicle A carried a surcharge of 5% instead, its share would be $600.00 plus $30.00, which is $630.00, and vehicle B's share would still be $500.00.

## Points of judgement

**Does an earned discount reduce the discount room left under the package's maximum total discount?**
No. A DriveSense adjustment is not part of the policy discount sum and does not count toward that maximum.

**Can a discount earned on one vehicle be applied to another vehicle the customer drives more?**
No. The adjustment belongs to the enrolled vehicle's share of the base premium and is never moved to another vehicle or averaged across the policy.

**Does a vehicle on a pay-per-mile program receive a participation discount?**
No. A vehicle on a pay-per-mile program takes no participation or earned discount.
